o: The student arrived this week: intake, the first week hour by hour, the K–5 kit, and what goes home.
k: Everything for the week a student arrives: Newcomer Intake (type the student once; the profile, plan and letter fill themselves), the Newcomer Week 1 Kit (the first week hour by hour, ending in an exit ticket), the Elementary Newcomer Kit for K–5, and the two things that go home — Your Guide to School in the U.S. in five languages and My First 100 Words at School. The front office's part is in the Front Office Kit.

o: The spring test from the teacher's side: the special issue, the task practice with keys, the Six Pies set.
k: The ELPT from the EL teacher's desk: the page-turning special issue with daily routines and sixteen test moves, the teacher edition of the ELPA21 task practice (read-aloud scripts, keys, look-fors, four lanes), and Six Southern Pies, one infographic that runs every task type across all four domains.

o: For the teacher who speaks no Spanish: a 90-minute workshop, a six-module course, the research guide, handouts, phrases, cognates.
k: Six pieces for the content teacher who speaks no Spanish: the 90-minute teacher-led workshop, the self-paced six-module course with audio, Using Spanish in the Content Classroom (the research-based guide for math, science, social studies and ELA), the Teacher Handout Folder (ten one-page handouts), Spoken Spanish & Spoken English (what you will hear and a reply for each), and Cognate Hunt (paste any reading; the words your Spanish speakers already know light up).

o: Every issue of the teacher magazine (No. 1 to No. 4), the Teaching the ELPT special issue, the student magazine, the bulletins and the Tech Radar, in one rack.
k: Every EL Publishing periodical in one rack. The teacher magazine: No. 1 Every Teacher (Sept 2026), No. 2 The Field Atlas (Oct), No. 3 The Language of Belonging (Nov), No. 4 The Language of Home (Dec, with a K–12 edition). The special issues: Christmas Around the World (36 pages, K–12, every subject) and Teaching the ELPT (24 pages, interactive). The student magazine Many Voices, Issue 1. Then the bulletins: The Language Bridge, What's New in Teaching English Learners (Field Notes, with evidence ratings) and the monthly EL Tech Radar. For the day-by-day version, read Today in EL.

o: Every piece of professional learning on the hub: the self-paced module, the taught session, the podcast, the book study, the literacy guide.
k: Every piece of professional learning on the hub: Every Teacher Is a Language Teacher (self-paced, six sections, fits a department meeting), The Session with Elena (Emerging and Progressing, taught), the Every Teacher podcast, Fifty Strategies, One Semester (a PLC book study), Improving Adolescent Literacy in plain English, and the PD Library index of 54 more pieces by grade and level.

o: Practice for every domain of the spring English test: interactive sets for reading, writing, listening and speaking, plus the full form and the question-types guide.
k: Every ELPT practice tool for students in one place, by domain. Reading: Storm Reading Sets (five interactive sets) and the ELPA21 Reading Studio under mock-test conditions. Writing: Storm Writing Sets (the five ELPA21 writing tasks with live self-checks). Listening: Storm Listening Sets (seven task types, a voice per speaker) and Listening Practice Sets 1 and 2. Speaking: Storm Speaking Sets (record, replay, self-check) and the Listening & Speaking Studio. All four domains: English On Your Own (a full form with every task type), the student Task Practice packet and the ELPA Question Types guide. Every Storm set has a teacher key at #key.

o: For the math or science teacher: the words that trip, the routines, the frames in four lanes, and the grid for every subject.
k: Subject-specific language support for content teachers. The Math Language Pack: a word-problem unpacker, the six families of words that trip, Three Reads, frames for explaining, justifying, comparing and critiquing, and fair assessment. The Science Language Pack: a lab report builder in four lanes, claim-evidence-reasoning frames, twenty words with another meaning outside science, Greek and Latin word parts with Spanish twins, and lab safety in English and Spanish with audio. By Subject & Grade: the language demand, two moves and what to use for every subject and grade band.

o: Run-ons, sentence features, the grammar map, calisthenics, grammar songs, and two writing coaches.
k: The sentence and the paragraph, seven ways: Storm Sentence Lab (stop writing run-ons), Sentence Lab (sixteen grammar features in real school scenes), The Grammar Map (grammar you can see), Storm Grammar Calisthenics (a bilingual coach, fifteen minutes a day), Grammar Beats (grammar as radio songs), The Writing Studio (Mr. Castillo teaches the shape of a 4 or 5) and Write About It (Ms. Bell's six-step routine).

o: Point at the thing, hear the word: three picture-dictionary issues and Storm Lens, the camera that names the room.
k: Vocabulary you can see and hear: The Picture Dictionary Issues 1–3 (twelve spreads each, Spanish, word and sentence audio, four activities per spread) and Storm Lens, which points a Chromebook at the room and turns it into the vocabulary list.

o: Full-period interactive lessons and readers for the 9–12 block: attention, tamales, a school day, a student magazine.
k: Full-period interactive lessons and readers for the 9–12 EL block: Your Attention Is for Sale, How Tamales Are Made (the feature article behind the sample lesson), School Life • Language Lab (twenty-five four-skill activities inside an ordinary school day) and Many Voices, the magazine written for multilingual high-school students.

o: Language or disability? The fair evaluation, who sits in the meeting, both plans on one page, how accommodations stack.
k: For EL teachers, special education teachers and IEP teams working with an English learner who has, or may have, a disability: a side-by-side table that separates second-language acquisition from signs of a possible disability, a twelve-point pre-referral checklist, what a fair evaluation looks like (native language, interpreters, norms), who has to be in the IEP meeting and a ten-point meeting check, a builder that prints the LSP and the IEP side by side on one page, how accommodations stack on MAAP and the ELPT including domain exemptions and the alternate assessment, the exit rule for dual-identified students, and family scripts in English and Spanish with audio.

o: A plain guide, a coach who teaches the daily lesson, and a learn-to-read program for teens.
k: Three phonics tools in one place. The Easy Guide to Teaching Phonics is a ten-minute read for any teacher: what to teach in order across nine stages, the 15-minute daily lesson, four routines (blending, sound boxes, dictation, decodable reading), the sounds Spanish speakers need extra time on, and quick checks and fixes. Phonics Coach teaches one 15-minute lesson aloud for each of 187 school days, with captions, coach's notes and a box for the teacher's own notes. Storm Readers is a Science of Reading program for grades 9-12 newcomers at ELPA21 Level 1: 120 lessons in eight stages with a recorded voice coach and 48 decodable readers written for teenagers. Free, no login; coach voices are synthesized. It lives on its own site.

o: Find what exists in a student's home language for English, math, history and science.
k: A searchable directory of 229 entries for English, math, history and science in elementary, middle and high school. Each entry says exactly what is in the student's language (the whole site, the student pages, subtitles only, or a paired text), the grades, the cost, and one way to use it with English learners. Spanish is covered level by level; a separate tab lists resources in Arabic, Vietnamese, Chinese and Haitian Creole, including glossaries, video lessons, storybooks and family tip sheets. Level tabs, subject filters, search, share buttons and an English/Spanish toggle. Entries marked 'Not rechecked' are home-page addresses to confirm before sharing. It lives on its own site.

o: Find the seam, pick the fix, stop writing run-ons — with a coach lab for the teacher.
k: A run-on clinic for grades 9–12 English learners, built on ELP Standard 10. Students tap the seam where a second idea begins, fix each run-on with a period, a comma + FANBOYS, a semicolon or a subordinator (and learn which fix fits the relationship), and paste their own paragraph into a checker that flags likely run-ons and comma splices. A Grammar Lab runs six stations (subjects and verbs, independent vs. dependent clauses, FANBOYS, subordinators, semicolons and transitions, sentence triage) with a coach lesson and one-chance questions; Sentence Surgery is a 60-second seam hunt and Combine-It Studio catches comma splices; a Daily Dose gives three sentences a day for 180 school days. Four lanes (Newcomer, Emerging, Progressing, Challenge), badges, a certificate, an exit ticket that copies or sends to a class form, and a student-controlled English/Spanish toggle for every direction and coach line. The Coach Lab gives teachers six 10-minute mini-lessons with a timer, Level 3 → Level 4 model pairs with what a rater sees, a class error log and a printable anchor chart. Free, no login, device voice; it lives on its own site.

o: Seven more listening lessons: new words, scenes, talks, debates and lectures.
k: A second complete set of interactive ELPA21-style listening practice for grades 9–12 English learners, in the same seven formats as Set 1 with all-new content. Listen and Match the Word (weather, food, school things, clothes); Listen and Match the Sentence (morning, weekend, at school, helping at home); Listen for Information (kitchen tools, weather tools, parts of a plant, a frogs-and-toads Venn diagram); Listen to a Conversation (a recycling poster project, a first job at a grocery store); Listen to a Debate (school uniforms, a four-day school week); Listen to the Student (a science presentation on the water cycle with slides and classmates' questions); Listen to the Teacher (the Mississippi River, sea turtles). Device voices, slow speed, show-text and show-words supports, one try per question in Lessons 4–7, original drawings and scripts, no account, nothing saved.

o: Students hear a direction, conversation, debate, presentation or lesson, then tap the picture, card or answer that matches.
k: Interactive ELPA21-style listening practice for grades 9–12 English learners, Unit 1 in seven lessons. Listen and Match the Word: four items (places, sky, ways to go, animals) where a spoken direction such as 'Point to the planet' asks students to tap the matching picture. Listen and Match the Sentence: four items of four scenes each (restaurant, in the car, home and town, trips) matched to a spoken sentence. Listen for Information: a short spoken passage on each of four pages (lab tools, liquids, soil layers, Alaska and Hawaii on a Venn diagram), then ten numbered directions students follow by tapping a card and tapping where it goes. Listen to a Conversation: two student conversations (a math assignment in the hallway, a school garden on the walk home), each followed by five read-aloud multiple-choice questions on main idea, detail, sequence, inference and prediction, with two device voices and a highlighted transcript. Listen to a Debate: two moderated student debates (a later school start time, a school-day phone ban) with eight questions, including check-all-that-apply and completing an argument-and-reasons graphic organizer. Listen to the Student: a history-class presentation on how Mississippi's state government is organized, with slides that build as the student speaks, two classmates who raise their hands to ask questions, and five questions including matching labels to the three branches. Listen to the Teacher: two science mini-lessons (how hurricanes form and weaken, how fireflies make cold light) with ten questions, including check-all-that-apply and choosing the correct picture. Device text-to-speech, a slow voice, show-text and show-words supports, instant feedback with retry, and a first-try score per item; original drawings and passages, no account, nothing saved.

o: Five ELPT-style reading sets on tabs: two stories, a data set, a science investigation and an argument essay.
k: Five interactive ELPT-style reading sets for grades 9–12 on one page with tabs: Storm Salsa and The Last Round (literary), Screens and Sleep (data analysis), The Pot-in-Pot Cooler (science investigation) and Fix It Yourself (argument essay). Drag-and-drop, hot spots, drop-downs, select-all and sentence selection; Practice and Test modes; read-aloud, glossary, Spanish directions; results to copy to the teacher; teacher key at #key.

o: The five ELPA21 writing tasks: fix the paragraph, write questions, answer an email, tell the storyboard, build a claim.
k: The five ELPA21 writing task types for grades 9–12 as interactive tabs: Fix the Paragraph (discrete editing), Ask the Pilot (writing questions), Reply to Jalen (respond to a peer email), The Empty Lot (storyboard) and Required to Serve? (construct a claim). Live self-checks as students type, sentence stems, Spanish directions, copy-my-writing for turning in; rubrics and model responses at #key.

o: Seven listening tasks with a voice for each speaker: match, listen for information, a debate, a conversation, a lecture, a presentation.
k: Seven ELPA21 listening task types for grades 9–12 as interactive tabs: Listen and Match sentences and words, Listen for Information, an academic debate, a short conversation, a lecture and discussion, and a student presentation. The browser speaks every stimulus with a different synthesized voice per speaker; transcripts are hidden in Test mode and each recording plays twice; teacher key with full scripts at #key.

o: Record, play back and self-check the four ELPA21 speaking tasks: compare pictures, a book report, a chart and a claim, observe and report.
f: Interactive · 4 task types · record and replay
k: Four ELPA21 speaking task types for grades 9–12 as interactive tabs: Compare Pictures, Language Arts Presentation, Analyze a Visual and a Claim, and Observe and Report. Students record in the browser, play back and download; recordings stay on the device; a live transcript feeds a self-check where the browser supports it; rubrics on the ELPA21 point scales and model responses at #key.

o: A read-aloud lesson where students feel the tricks apps use on them, then take their attention back.
k: A bilingual (EN/ES) 90-minute reading lesson for grades 9–12 on the attention economy: a bell ringer with a sketchpad, a hook, a fake feed that lets students feel infinite scroll, the red badge and the variable reward for sixty seconds, a six-paragraph read-aloud with sentence-by-sentence highlighting, tap-to-define vocabulary with Spanish, stop-and-jot pauses, an app-design task, vocabulary matching with streaks, five auto-graded ELPA21-style items with a practice level, an O·R·E·A·C exit ticket sent to the teacher, and an attention-check lock that only a teacher code opens.

t: Your Guide to School in the U.S.
o: How an American school works, for a family that arrived this week.
k: For any K–12 student new to an American school: how schools work, enrolling, a school day, grades and graduation, legal rights and EL support, classroom culture, family tips and a 60-word glossary — English side by side with Spanish, Vietnamese, Arabic, Chinese or Haitian Creole. Free PDF in each language.

o: The hundred words of a first month, tap to hear, printable as flashcards.
k: The words a newcomer hears in the first month — people, places, the schedule, teacher instructions, lunch, rules, grades and asking for help — ten groups of ten, with tap-to-hear pronunciation, two quiz modes, a progress counter and printable flashcards. Five languages.

o: Point a Chromebook at the room and the room becomes the vocabulary list.
k: Point the Chromebook camera at anything in the room and the room becomes the vocabulary list. Two recognition models run in the browser (80 objects live, 1,000 on scan) against a 334-word school bank; every word opens a card with Spanish, the cognate flag, four-lane sentence frames, a verb collocation, pronunciation coaching for Spanish speakers, plurals, a quick check, an ELPA21-style “describe the picture” speaking task and a write-it check — all speech-checked. The student's own photos become their word wall, four practice modes, scavenger missions and rolling end credits. Narrated like a film. Teachers get hunt links, a class view from student files, an exit ticket and a device check. Installs and works offline. No account, nothing uploaded.

o: Verb jumps, error hunts, rapid fire, dictation sprints — a bilingual coach, fifteen minutes a day.
k: Coach Marisol, a bilingual EL Specialist, runs a 15–20 minute grammar workout at the start of every class — and nobody sits still. Each day opens with a body move tied to a grammar decision (verb jumps, stand-or-sit judgments, stomp the stress, wall sits chanting the rule), then sets and reps said out loud, error hunts where students tap the wrong word, partner volleys on a five-second clock, chain drills, four corners, dictation sprints checked by the browser, and a ninety-second pressure write before three exit checks. Thirty-six weeks climb ELP Standard 10 from plurals and the verb be to passive voice, relative clauses, conditionals and academic transitions, with a Spanish bridge every Wednesday. Emerging students fill frames while Progressing students transform sentences, side by side. Projector mode, English and Spanish speech, a Today button that knows the week, a Friday certificate. No account; everything stays on the Chromebook.

o: ELPA21 practice a student can do alone — speaking checked by the browser.
k: Built to the published ELPA21 grades 9–12 blueprint: all twenty-two task types — Listen and Match, Academic Debate, Short Conversation, Argument and Support Essay, Discrete Editing, Construct a Claim, Compare Pictures, Observe and Report and the rest — plus a sixty-item full practice form (23 listening, 26 reading, 5 writing, 6 speaking) that returns a level estimate per domain and an Emerging / Progressing / Proficient determination. Speaking records and checks what the student actually said; writing gets an automatic check and the rater's checklist. Directions in six languages. No account, no teacher needed.

o: Credits, state tests and a four-year plan, filled in with a counselor.
k: Pick a diploma path (Traditional, CTE, Academic, Distinguished), type the credits you have and watch the meters, check off the four state tests, learn how home-country classes and your first language count, and fill in a four-year plan with your counselor. Five languages.

t: The English Test, Explained for Families
o: What the ELPT measures, what the levels mean, how a student exits.
k: What the ELPT (ELPA21) is, the four domains, what Levels 1–5 actually mean, a sample score report decoded, the exit rule (Level 4 in all four), the EL year calendar, and what families can do at home — in five languages.

o: Eighty “I can” statements a student scores three times a year.
k: Eighty “I can…” statements across listening, speaking, reading and writing at Levels 1–5. Students check what is true today, see an estimated level per skill, set a goal for each, and copy a summary for their teacher — a mirror of the ELPT they can use three times a year. Five languages.

t: Sentence Lab: English Grammar in Real Life
o: Sixteen grammar features in real school scenes, two lanes on every page.
k: Sixteen grammar features in realistic school scenes — subject and verb, pronouns, be, articles, plurals, adjectives, present, negatives, questions, right now, past, future plans, prepositions, connectors, sentence repair, expansion — with a Newcomer lane and a Progressing lane on every page. A shared writing project, a before/after six-skill check, and the full teacher key with a scoring rubric. Free 25-page PDF.

o: Practice written in the exact format of the test, all four domains.
k: Sixteen pages of practice across all four domains, written in the format of the assessment: construct a claim, respond to a message, observe and report, state an opinion, follow instructions, academic lecture, informational set, short paragraph.

o: Point at the thing, hear the word, say it, spell it, use it. Twelve places, drawn as spreads.
k: A magazine-style picture dictionary, Issue 1: twelve illustrated spreads for the places a secondary newcomer walks through every week, the classroom, the school, the kitchen, the bedroom, the grocery store, the clinic, the body, clothes, downtown, the weather, jobs and feelings. 144 words, each with the Spanish, a spoken pronunciation and a spoken example sentence; tap a number on the picture or a word on the list and both light up. Four activities on every spread: Listen and find, Spell it, Use it (the sentence with the word missing) and Say it (record on the device, compare with the model). Eight of ten stamps the spread. Each spread prints as two clean pages for a wall or a binder. Original flat-vector scenes drawn for the issue; synthesized voices, labeled as such.

o: Food, the living room, the road, the bank, the clock, the family, the gym, the screen, the farm: twelve new spreads.
k: Issue 2 of the magazine-style picture dictionary: twelve new illustrated spreads, food, the living room, the bathroom, transportation, money and the bank, time and the calendar, the twelve classroom verbs, the family, sports and PE, technology, the restaurant and the farm. 144 more words, each with the Spanish, a spoken pronunciation and a spoken sentence; tap a number on the picture or a word on the list and both light up. The same four activities on every spread (Listen and find, Spell it, Use it, Say it), a stamp at eight of ten, and a print button for the wall. Original flat-vector scenes drawn for the issue; synthesized voices, labeled as such.

o: The lab, shapes, colors, the yard, a whole day of verbs, opposites, animals, safety, the park, the arts: twelve more spreads.
k: Issue 3 of the magazine-style picture dictionary moves from places to ideas: the science lab, shapes and measurement, colors, the house and yard, a whole day of routine verbs, describing people, opposites in pairs, animals, safety and emergencies, the park, celebrations, and arts and music. 144 more words, each with the Spanish, a spoken pronunciation and a spoken sentence; tap a number on the picture or a word on the list and both light up. The same four activities on every spread (Listen and find, Spell it, Use it, Say it), a stamp at eight of ten, and a print button for the wall. Original flat-vector scenes drawn for the issue; synthesized voices, labeled as such.

o: Grammar you can see: a sentence X-ray, four lines, fourteen taught stations, a stamp at each.
k: Basic English grammar as a map a student travels: fourteen stations on four lines, from the capital letter and the eight parts of speech through determiners, verb tenses, agreement, adverbs, prepositions, conjunctions, interjections, the sentence and punctuation. A Sentence X-ray on the cover colors every word by its job, with the Spanish term a tap away. At each station Ms. Reyes, an animated teacher with a synthesized voice, teaches the lesson at a chalkboard; then a short Know it in plain English, examples with the target underlined, and eight self-checking items (tap the word, choose, or type). Seven of eight stamps the station. Written for Newcomer and Emerging students in grades 6–12 with the Spanish-speaker traps called out; Progressing students clear the map and move to the Writing Studio. Original lessons and items; progress stays on the device.

o: Mr. Castillo teaches the shape of a 4 or 5: claim, reasons, transitions, the email, the edit, the clock.
k: Eight writing lessons taught at a chalkboard by Mr. Castillo, an animated teacher with a synthesized voice, for English learners in grades 6–12 aiming at a 4 or 5 on the ELPA21 writing test. Each lesson is an I-do, we-do, you-do: he writes on the board while thinking aloud, asks the class to choose, asks each student for one line in a notebook and checks it against the features a scorer looks for, and in lesson 8 runs a full timed response with a plan box, a clock, a self-score and a level-5 model with the reasons it scores. The claim; reasons and evidence; transitions and their commas; compare and contrast; the formal email; editing like a scorer; the timed response. Projector mode and a mute switch let a teacher be the voice and teach from the board; the full script is printable. Writing stays on the device; a copy button sends it to a document for the teacher.

t: ELPA Question Types: Test Prep Guide
o: What each question is really asking, the words that signal it, three moves, and a worked example with every choice explained.
k: A test prep guide to the 18 question types on English language proficiency tests such as the ELPA21: main idea, key details, cause and effect, sequence, summarize, vocabulary in context, reference words, complete a sentence, inference, text evidence, author's purpose, paragraph purpose, comparison, character or speaker, feelings and motives, identify a picture, analyze a visual, and understand an explanation. Each type has a plain-language description of what it is really asking, the stem wording that signals it, three moves that work, the trap wrong answers use, and an original worked example (a short passage, picture or graph) where tapping a choice explains why it is right or wrong; a second quick item follows. A five-step routine and the four shapes of wrong answers open the guide, and a one-page quick reference closes it. A Read it aloud button turns any example into a listening item, and a printable PDF with the full answer key is included. All passages are original; the guide is not affiliated with any test publisher.

o: Ms. Bell teaches the six-step routine on four given topics (describe, explain how, tell a time, opinion) and then any topic you bring.
k: Five writing lessons taught at a chalkboard by Ms. Bell, an animated teacher with a synthesized voice, for English learners in grades 6–12. Lessons 1–4 each take one real prompt and teach one kind of writing from first look to last period: describe a place, explain how to do something, tell about a time, and give an opinion. Every lesson uses the same six-step routine, read it, brainstorm it, plan it, open it, build it, close it and check it, so students learn a method they can run on any prompt. She writes each sentence on the board while thinking aloud, asks the class to choose (find the off-topic note, pick the correct sentence), asks each student for one line in a notebook and checks it, and ends with a 15-minute timed response with five plan boxes, a clock, a self-score and a model with the reasons it works. Lesson 5 teaches the job words in a prompt and walks students through their own topic. Her voice is synthesized and every line is original; student writing stays on the device. Teachers can project it, mute her and teach from the script, and print the script.

o: Hear it twice, choose, check; then record your answer and compare it with a model.
k: ELPA21-style listening and speaking practice a student can do alone on a phone. Four units (six Southern pies, first week at a new school, storms over the Gulf, three branches of government), each with the three listening formats of the test, Listen and Match, Short Conversation and Academic Lecture, heard at most twice at a natural pace, with the transcript and the reason for the answer after every item; and two speaking tasks in the Observe and Report, Give the Steps, Classroom Chat and Opinion formats, recorded on the student's own device, self-checked against three lines, then compared with a model answer. Frames in four lanes under every prompt; a Support switch for unlimited listens, slower speed and early transcripts. All voices synthesized and labeled as such; recordings never leave the device. Teacher section with transcripts, key and alignment. 48 listening items, 8 speaking tasks. Grades 6–12.

o: ELPT-style reading practice under mock-test conditions, six grade bands.
k: Mississippi ELPT-style reading practice for English learners: six grade bands, 122 original items, eight item types, mock-test conditions, accommodations, bilingual supports, levels, badges and a teacher dashboard.

o: Twenty-five four-skill activities set inside an ordinary school day.
k: Twenty-five four-skill ELPA21-style activities built around school-life scenarios: reading, listening, speaking and writing in the format students will see on the test.

o: Grammar as radio songs, each with a lesson built to the beat.
k: Radio-style grammar songs with full interactive lessons: nouns, adjectives and verbs, each with an audio track and a student lesson built to the beat.

o: The feature article behind the sample lesson, with five activities.
k: Feature article plus five interactive activities, vocabulary matching and a student progress report. The text behind the sample-lesson breakdown.

o: A magazine written for multilingual high-school students.
k: A magazine for multilingual high-school students: articles, interactive features, vocabulary tools and a teacher resource page.

o: Paste a word problem and see the words that trip; then Three Reads, frames in four lanes and a six-minute vocabulary routine.
k: For math teachers with English learners: a word-problem unpacker (paste any problem; it marks words that change the operation or mean something different outside math, with the Spanish), six families of words that trip (reversal words like less than, everyday words with a math meaning, small words that carry the operation, comparisons, sound-alikes, conditions and passives), math cognates, the Three Reads routine in four lanes, sentence frames for explaining steps, justifying, comparing and critiquing reasoning, a six-minute vocabulary routine, and fair assessment that keeps the math and removes the extra English.

o: A lab report frame for every lane, claim-evidence-reasoning, twenty words that mislead, and lab safety in two languages.
f: Language pack · Lab frames · 4 lanes · EN/ES
k: For science teachers with English learners: a lab report builder that prints a frame for the Newcomer, Emerging, Progressing or Challenge lane with a word bank, claim-evidence-reasoning (CER) frames in four lanes, twenty words with a different meaning outside science (theory, matter, solution, force, work), a routine for any new term, sixteen Greek and Latin word parts with Spanish cognates, twelve lab safety lines in English and Spanish with audio, and fair assessment that grades the science separately from the English.

o: Need something for your English learners that is not here? Tap, type a sentence, send.
k: A one-minute request form: tap your role, grade band, subject and the kind of thing that would help, add a sentence about what you need for your English learners, and send it by email or copy the text. Requests shape what gets built next; what is built goes on the hub free for everyone. Suggest a resource, ask for a tool, contact.

t: Today in EL: the Daily Feed
o: Updated every morning: three picks with a take and a move to try, plus thirty days of EL pedagogy and articles worth your time.
k: The hub's daily page. Every morning at 4:40 Central a script in the hub's repository reads thirteen public feeds — Colorín Colorado, Larry Ferlazzo, Language Magazine, the Immigrant Learning Center, The Conversation, Cult of Pedagogy, Hechinger, Chalkbeat, MindShift, NPR Education, EdSurge, The 74 and Mississippi Today — keeps thirty days, and sorts items into English-learner pedagogy and articles of interest to any teacher, with Mississippi mentions flagged. A separate morning run chooses three picks and writes a short take and one move to try tomorrow for each. Searchable, filterable by source, printable.

o: For the registrar: enroll a family that speaks no English — today, legally, kindly — with the board, the survey and the clock.
k: For registrars and school secretaries: the first ten minutes with a family that does not speak English, an “I speak…” board in fourteen languages, the Home Language Survey in six languages, twenty counter phrases with Spanish audio, an identification clock that works out when the screener and parent notice are due, and an interpreter request form. Plyler enrollment rules and Title VI language access in plain words.

o: A bilingual parent conference for an EL: interpreter checklist, the script with audio, the report card explained, a take-home summary.
k: For any teacher meeting the family of an English learner: an interpreter checklist and bilingual invitation, a fifteen-minute conference script in English and Spanish with a speaker on every line, the report card explained in fourteen bilingual terms, six questions for the family to ask (and what to say when they do not understand), and a builder that prints a one-page English/Spanish take-home summary with the four levels, the help in class and one thing to do at home.

o: Paste a rubric or a quiz; get the version that grades the content, with the English handled separately, in four lanes.
k: For content teachers: paste any rubric and the page splits content criteria from language criteria with a lane-fair expectation for each (flip any line); paste a quiz and it names each question type, flags negative stems, idioms, long stems and passive voice, and writes the four-lane version with a sample fair answer per lane; score one piece of work with content and language apart and get the margin note and grade-book comment. The legal basis on one page.

o: The forty questions content teachers actually ask about ELs, answered in a hundred words, with the rule and the tool.
k: Forty questions teachers of biology, algebra and history actually ask about English learners — can I take off points for grammar, can she use Google Translate on the test, why is he still an EL after three years, should I tell the family to speak English at home, can an EL be in honors, what do I actually have to do — each answered in about a hundred words, with the rule behind it where there is one and the hub tool that finishes the job. Searchable, filterable by topic, printable.

t: Read Your Roster: the ELPA21 Level Decoder
o: Your roster says Level 2. Here is what that student can do in your class, what is fair to grade, and what MAAP allows.
k: For the content teacher handed a class list with ELPT levels next to the names. Tap a student's four domain levels (Listening, Speaking, Reading, Writing) and get the ELPA21 status, the hub's lane, what the student can do in your biology, algebra or history class right now and what that looks like, which assessment formats are a fair measure of content and which still measure English, the accommodations Mississippi allows on MAAP for that profile with the LSP wording, three moves for tomorrow, a printable profile card, a Watch-the-level scene for each domain (what a Level 2 reads, hears, says and writes, then the scaffold), and a growth projector against the exit line. Paste a whole roster and see the class by lane, the domain averages, the lowest domain and what it means for planning. A third tab explains the five levels, the Emerging / Progressing / Proficient rule, the Mississippi exit line and four things a roster cannot tell you. Nothing leaves the browser.

o: Self-paced from names and greetings to the family call: audio phrases, self-checking practice, quizzes, cheat sheets, a printable workbook and a certificate.
k: A free six-module course for K–12 teachers of math, science, social studies, ELA, the arts and every other subject who have little or no Spanish and teach Spanish-speaking English learners. Module 1 teaches the sound rules and two-surname system so every name on a roster is said right; Module 2 covers greetings and when to use tú with a student and usted with a parent; Module 3 the classroom directions a class hears every day, to one student or to all; Module 4 specific praise, support after a mistake, checking understanding without ¿Entiendes?, and well-being check-ins with clear limits on when to get help; Module 5 cognates, false cognates, bilingual sentence frames, Talk Then Write and Preview-View-Review; Module 6 the good-news family call, opening a conference, and when a qualified interpreter must take over — never a student, and never a question about immigration status. Every module has learning goals, a mini-lesson, a phrase table with a say-it key and browser Spanish audio, a cultural and teaching tip, self-checking practice, a five-question quiz, and a one-page cheat sheet; progress saves on the device and ends in three role-play stations, a rubric and a printable certificate. A 64-page workbook with the answer key downloads as PDF or Word.

o: A teacher-led workshop for colleagues who speak no Spanish: names, directions, encouragement, the call home.
k: A free 90-minute workshop any teacher can lead for colleagues who speak no Spanish — no outside trainer. Eight timed blocks: five pronunciation rules that make Spanish readable (pure vowels, the stress rule, silent h and j-as-h, r versus rr) with a name card of eighteen common first and last names; Round 1 greetings and students' names; Round 2 the eighteen directions a class hears every day, to one student or to everyone, plus numbers for pages and groups, practiced as Simón dice; Round 3 encouragement and check-in phrases with a cut-apart card deck; Round 4 listening for the fifteen things students most often say to a teacher; Round 5 a two-minute good-news family call in formal usted, rehearsed back to back; the cognate shortcut with five converting endings and nine false friends; and a pocket card, exit ticket and six ten-minute follow-ups. Every phrase has a say-it key and plays in the browser's Spanish voice; a runner times each block and a projector mode puts phrases on the screen one at a time. Fifteen-page facilitator packet as a free PDF.

t: Using Spanish in the Content Classroom
o: Research-based moves for math, science, social studies and ELA teachers who speak no Spanish: cognates, talk-then-write, fair assessment.
k: A 40-page practical guide for grades 9–12 content teachers who do not speak Spanish. Chapter 1 lays out the research (Cummins on transfer, Moll's funds of knowledge, García's translanguaging, the cognate studies) and the legal floor; Chapter 2 separates long-term English learners from newcomers and gives a five-question language survey; Chapter 3 teaches cognate spelling patterns with four subject lists (math, science, social studies, ELA) and sixteen false friends; then bilingual word walls and glossaries, Talk → Plan → Write, Preview-View-Review, strategic pairing, eighteen bilingual sentence frames, translation tools used well, honoring Spanish in assessment, a teacher's Spanish phrase bank, family partnership, eleven common pitfalls, a lesson snapshot for Algebra I, Biology, U.S. History and English II, a 30-day plan, a one-page quick reference and planning tools. Fully referenced; free PDF.

o: Ten one-page handouts from the guide: cognate lists by subject, the phrase bank, frames by level, newcomer week one, a family call script.
k: Ten printable one-page handouts that accompany Using Spanish to Teach Spanish-Speaking English Learners in the Content Classroom. A quick-reference page of ten strategies with the two-question test; cognate lists for math, science, social studies and ELA — true cognates, words to pre-teach, and the false friends with what the Spanish word really means (celda, éxito, carácter, librería, billón); a teacher Spanish phrase bank with directions to one student and to the class, encouragement, check-ins, and a one-minute pronunciation key; bilingual sentence frames with Emerging full frames beside Progressing academic frames for discussing and writing, plus one frame per subject; a newcomer first-week checklist with a five-question language survey; a seven-step good-news family call script in formal usted with a voicemail and when to request an interpreter; and a do's-and-don'ts page on using the home language. Every page has side tabs and a back-to-folder link, so the PDF works on a screen as well as printed.

o: Spot the key words, say what you need to find, read and prove it — in two languages.
k: A three-step comprehension move for English learners, connected to the Science of Reading: spot the key words in the question, say what you need to find using a sentence frame, then read for meaning and prove it with highlighted evidence in a complete sentence. A bilingual English–Spanish key for why, what, how, which, when and where; a worked example from question to answer; the Scarborough's Reading Rope connection (vocabulary, language structures, verbal reasoning); the move in four lanes. One printable poster, free PDF.

o: Three questions every content teacher asks, each answered with a free tool.
k: The front door for a teacher who teaches biology, math or history and has English learners in the room. Three questions — what do I do Monday, how do I grade them, am I allowed to change the test — each answered with a free tool, plus what the moves look like by subject, a spreadsheet of the resources sorted by when you need them, and the twelve things built for a content classroom.

o: A PLC book study of Herrell & Jordan's 50 Strategies, built for the teacher who teaches biology, not English.
k: An eight-session PLC book study of Herrell and Jordan's 50 Strategies for Teaching English Language Learners (6th ed., Pearson), written for content teachers. Every session is a 45-minute agenda: a five-minute opener nobody needs the reading to answer, a bring-back of last week's try-it with evidence, four discussion questions aimed at what we would do in our rooms, one strategy to try before the next session with a look-for, and a one-sentence exit. All fifty strategies are covered in eight themed sessions (anxiety and input, vocabulary, reading the textbook, writing and talk, questions and checks, planning for language, grouping, data and support), each paired with one hub resource. A strategy finder tags all fifty by what they do, which subjects they fit and which are fast to try; a try-it log stays on the teacher's device and copies into a doc; eight checked sessions unlock a printable certificate. Quotes nothing from the book; the facilitator guide covers norms, credit hours and Title III evidence.

o: Elena, an animated presenter, teaches what to change for each level.
k: An eight-minute professional-development session for content teachers, taught on screen by Elena — the EL specialist from the Every Teacher podcast as an animated, lip-synced presenter. What the words Emerging (ELPT levels 1–2) and Progressing (3–4) mean and why to ask for the four domain scores; what a student at each level can already do in a biology, algebra or history class and where each one stalls; the trap for each; the five things you change for an Emerging student (five words first, show everything twice, frames with a word bank, check by showing, home language as a bridge) and the five for a Progressing student (unpack one sentence a day, frames that push, tier-two words, talk before writing, wait time); what output looks like and what you grade at each level; one cell-parts lesson taught in two sizes; and a ten-minute planning routine. Captioned, with chapters, a clickable transcript, MP4 download and a run-it-as-PD plan for a department meeting.

o: A taught session, the Six Moves videos, and 54 more pieces of PD by grade and level.
k: A professional-learning library for the biology, algebra and history teacher with English learners. It opens with a ten-minute PD session on Emerging and Progressing students taught by Elena, an animated presenter, then Six Moves, a captioned video series — one classroom move in under three minutes each: Five Words First, Frames in Four Lanes, Unpack One Sentence, Word Bank–Frame–Model, Check Without Asking, Grade the Content — then 54 more pieces of PD on eight shelves — start here, make it understandable, get them talking, reading in the content area, writing, assess and grade fairly, newcomers and families, tools and AI — filterable by grade band K–2 through 9–12, language level (Emerging, Progressing, Proficient/monitored), kind (watch, listen, do, read, print, plan) and time. Every piece is under an hour and ends with the thing to do in your own classroom. Seven guided paths (your first ninety minutes, a six-week PLC, a newcomer arrives Monday, elementary, secondary, fluent-but-stalling, exited-and-slipping), a done-list that stays in the browser, and a printable PD log for district records. Sixteen items are from outside EL Publishing, each one verified.

o: Six five-minute conversations on strengthening English in a content class.
k: Six audio episodes, five to six minutes each, for the biology, algebra and history teacher with English learners in the room: who is in your room (what Emerging and Progressing students can do), making a lesson understandable without watering it down, structured talk with sentence frames by level, reading the textbook, writing that actually happens, and grading the content rather than the English — plus the Language Service Plan and the five people who can help. Two synthesized voices, a content teacher and an EL specialist; full transcripts, two discussion questions per episode for a department meeting, MP3 downloads and an RSS feed for any podcast app.

o: Paste any reading; the words your Spanish speakers already know light up.
k: Paste tomorrow's reading — a biology paragraph, a history passage, a word problem — and every English–Spanish cognate lights up, so a content teacher can see at a glance how much of the text their Spanish speakers already own. Certain pairs (373 school words, science and history heaviest) get a solid line; pattern guesses (-tion → -ción) get a dotted one and say so; false friends — library, exit, once, realize — are flagged in red with what the Spanish word really means. Prints a cognate wall, copies as a list, sends nothing anywhere. The tool for Monday Move 10.

o: Your subject, your grade band: the language demand, two moves, what to use.
k: Sixteen squares — English/ELA, mathematics, science and social studies crossed with K–2, 3–5, 6–8 and 9–12 — each naming what the language, not the content, asks of an English learner at that point, two moves from the Monday Moves series, and the hub resources that apply. Under every subject, twenty-seven free resources from elsewhere — the Library of Congress, Stanford, WIDA, PhET, the National Archives — each opened and checked before it was listed, with any free-account catch stated. Color-coded, narrowable to your band, printable.

t: Sheltered: 12 Minutes as an English Learner
o: Sit a real lesson in a language you don't speak. Then sit it again with supports.
k: Take a real Biology, Algebra I or U.S. History lesson in a language you do not speak — Spanish, Vietnamese or Arabic — then take it again with the four lanes in place. Same language, same clock, parallel questions. Your two scores end up side by side, each support is named with the lane it serves, and the last screen finally tells you what the lesson said. Built to run with a whole faculty in twenty-five minutes.

o: Four prompts to paste: scaffold a lesson, level a text, fix a quiz, write home.
k: Four copy-and-paste assistants for the teacher who teaches biology, not English: scaffold a lesson by lane, level a text and prep the vocabulary, make a quiz measure content instead of English (Mississippi accommodations built in), and write to families in English and Spanish. Works in Claude, Gemini, ChatGPT or Copilot; no student names ever.

o: Pick a standard, count your English learners, get five things to do.
k: For the teacher who teaches biology, algebra or history and has English learners on the roster, with no EL training needed. Three plain steps: pick a Mississippi standard (454 across ELA, math, science and social studies, kindergarten to grade 12), tap in your English learners by what you see and hear in class, and get five things to do, each with the reason it helps: the words to teach first, sentence starters in English and Spanish, where to seat students, how to make the reading easier, and one question to check each student. Then add extras one step at a time: lesson ideas, the lesson part by part, a daily leveled text with Spanish, example texts and free text builders, discussion questions and an exit ticket, a student choice board, a supports tracker, and a teach mode with a timer. The last step puts it all together in one plan to print or copy. Everything is tap or choose from a list; no typing, no account, no AI.

o: A Mississippi standard in; a four-lane lesson, leveled text or MAAP items out.
k: Pick a Mississippi standard (K–12 ELA, math, science, or Algebra I, Biology I, English II), describe the lesson you already teach, and get it back in four lanes: Newcomer, Emerging, Progressing, Challenge. Also writes leveled texts with text-dependent questions and MAAP-style items with a linguistically accessible twin for every item. Builds the prompt, you run it in Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini or Copilot, paste the answer back, and it lays out the plan. No sign-up on this site.

o: The whole obligation in plain language, for staff who never trained for it.
k: Plain-language guide for general-education, special-education and administrative staff: identification, instruction, assessment and the legal obligations, with strategies you can use tomorrow.

o: Paste a reading or upload a PDF: vocabulary with Spanish, hard sentences, a handout.
k: The Teacher Literacy Lab helps EL and content teachers teach the reading they already planned. Start here: paste tomorrow's reading, press one button, and get a 10-minute lesson in three steps (five words to say first with Spanish matches, the hardest sentence highlighted with questions to ask and good answers, and a sentence frame for students to finish), then press Teach it and read the slides aloud, print one page with a student half-sheet, or copy a language objective for the lesson plan. More options adds a tap-to-cut sentence cutter, printable sentence strips, and color-coded moves for ELPA21 Emerging (Levels 1–2) and Progressing (Levels 3–4). Word Check is a vocabulary analyzer: it sorts a reading into everyday, school and subject words, picks the words to teach first, finds Spanish cognates and false friends, words with a second meaning in class and word parts, and prints a word wall. Text X-Ray marks long sentences, passive voice, process nouns, logic words and pointing words, with teacher moves tagged to the Mississippi ELP and MS CCRS literacy standards and a student handout. Juicy Sentence Studio has 144 original sentences, one a week for 36 weeks in Biology I, U.S. History, Algebra I and English II, in English and Spanish, with printable cards, a student link and a Monday Moves card for every week. The juicy sentence method is boiled down to one page: Read it, Break it, Make it. The Teacher Writes Too is a 12-session PLC with a facilitator kit and certificate. English and Spanish interface, Midnight theme, no account.

o: One move, every room, five minutes: a weekly language move for any content class.
k: Monday Moves is a weekly staff series for content teachers of English learners, tagline “One move, every room, five minutes.” Thirty-seven one-page moves in four quarters plus a New Moves section: post and say the language goal, preview three words, sentence frames, talk before writing, checking without “Do you understand?”, cognate hunts, word parts, annotation, partner talk, growing sentences, feedback, ELPA21 season, test-question language, the home language as a tool, newcomers in spring, and the new Move 37, Stronger and Clearer Each Time (explain an answer to two partners, then rewrite it). Each move has why it works, three to five steps, examples by department, a version for each of the four lanes (Newcomer, Emerging, Progressing, Challenge), a try-it-this-week and what a visitor would see. Titles in English and Spanish, read-aloud, and designed PDF packets for each quarter plus the Move 37 card.

t: Improving Adolescent Literacy, in Plain English
o: The federal reading guide's five moves, on one folded sheet any teacher can use.
k: A free trifold brochure that turns the What Works Clearinghouse practice guide Improving Adolescent Literacy: Effective Classroom and Intervention Practices (IES, 2008) into plain English for teachers in grades 4–12. The five recommendations with their evidence ratings: teach vocabulary on purpose (strong), show students how good readers think through explicit comprehension strategy instruction (strong), extended discussion of what the text means (moderate), motivation and engagement through goals, choice and relevance (moderate), and intensive intervention for struggling readers by trained specialists (strong). Each move has how-to steps and a note for teachers of English learners; a Monday-morning checklist, the fine print and the full citation complete it. Printable two-sided PDF.

o: 150 frames by function and level, each with a Spanish gloss. Copy into a slide.
k: 150 frames by language function — narrate, inform, explain, argue, classroom talk — and by level 1–5, each with a Spanish gloss. Filter to today's function and your students' levels, tick the ones you want, copy them into your slide.

o: What you will hear from a Spanish speaker, and a useful reply for each.
k: Shared strengths, different patterns: what the two languages share, where sounds and sentences differ, what you may hear in class and a helpful response for each. Phrase banks in English and Spanish by lane, a correct-now-or-later decision guide, three practice cases, a twelve-error table, and a first-week belonging routine. Free 23-page PDF.

o: How to do it tomorrow, whether MAAP allows it, and the wording for the LSP.
k: Eighteen cards: what the accommodation is, who it fits, how to do it in class tomorrow, whether it is allowed on MAAP and ELPT, and the exact wording for the LSP. Filter by state-test-allowed, classroom-only, newcomer, reading, writing. Prints two-up.

o: One page for the substitute, one for the paraprofessional. No student names.
k: A one-page “English learners in this room” card for the substitute (lane counts, allowed supports, what to do and not do, no names) and a one-page guide for the paraprofessional or tutor working one-on-one: eight moves, a 20-minute session, a log, Spanish phrases.

o: Content and language objectives on one page, with six co-teaching models.
k: Content objective + language objective on one page, with a language-objective bank by subject and function, six co-teaching models, who-does-what, supports by lane, and separate assessments for content and language. Fills in the browser, prints on one page.

o: The first ten days with a young newcomer, and the printables for tomorrow.
k: The first ten days with a young newcomer, in two bands: what to get right each day, room setup, what transfers from the home language, and the printables for the desk tomorrow — picture-schedule and “I need” cards, 20 phrases, a family call script, a week-one show-me check. English and Spanish.

o: What other Mississippi teachers made with these tools and chose to share.
k: Real adaptations, leveled texts, and item sets Mississippi teachers made with EL Bridge and the Assistants and chose to share. Filter by subject, open the materials, add your own through the short form.

t: Six New Tech Tools for English Learners
o: What is new and free this month, with a classroom use for each lane.
k: Verified this month: Gemini in Google Classroom student study tools (newest, Oct 6), Read Along in Google Classroom, SpeakingMonkey, MinuteMic, Brisk Boost and Google Translate Practice — what's new, what it costs, a four-lane classroom use for each, and a watch list.

o: The monthly one-page bulletin for content teachers: five findings, five moves.
k: A one-page bulletin for content teachers: five findings from acquisition research with a classroom move attached to each, the eight SIOP components translated for a content classroom, paired content and language objectives, and a compliance corner.

t: Christmas Around the World · Special Edition
o: Eight December traditions, a 15-day countdown, coloring pages and state test prep, for every teacher in the building.
k: Christmas Around the World, the special December 2026 edition for every teacher, grades K–12, on customs only (what people make, cook, carry and light): an eight-stop world tour to read (Las Posadas, the parol, tamales at midnight, las patinatas, the fanal, Genna, the twelve dishes, the crown of candles) with words to teach and a move for grades 6–12 and K–5; a December greeting in fourteen languages; one lesson for any grade in four lanes; a 15-school-day countdown calendar with a practice for each band, a coaching note and a note for the teacher; coaching notes by domain; four coloring pages with a sentence to trace; listen-and-circle for K–2 and a reading page for grades 3–5; an eight-page black-and-white ELPA21 practice insert for grades 6–12 with listening scripts, a teacher key and a family interview in English and Spanish; Mississippi ELA standards K–12 and eight whole-class ELA activities for the general education teacher; one activity for every subject (math, science, social studies, art, music, PE, career and technical, technology, library, homeroom); five moves for any teacher; and state test prep (MAAP-style practice) for math grades 3–8 and Algebra I, science grades 5 and 8 and Biology, and U.S. History, with a key and the language of the test. Holiday, winter, Christmas, traditions, coloring sheets, countdown.

o: The December issue: the home language as a bridge, fifteen lessons, a K–12 edition, teacher keys.
k: The December 2026 issue of the EL Publishing English Learner Magazine for grades 9–12, themed The Language of Home: an editor's letter on the first language as a bridge, a two-page teaching feature (name it, compare it, carry it) with Emerging, Progressing and Extension supports, a December-with-care page on light and observances with three questions before any holiday lesson, a reading lab (The Window on Pine Street), a voice studio with a radio-style listening script and a 60-second speaking task, a language workshop on used to / now and time connectors plus word families, a literary lens (The Second Key), a procedural-writing workshop and a visual-literacy page with daylight data from eight cities, community pages with the Home Language Wall project and a bilingual family interview, a 90-minute block plus fifteen lessons for the three weeks before break, an original check with rubric and growth log, teacher keys, sources, and a five-day closing challenge. A K–12 edition (pages 26–29) runs the same routine for K–2, 3–5 and 6–8 with original readings, language targets, speaking and writing tasks, family notes and a five-lesson week each. Web page with every page previewed, plus the free 30-page PDF. Includes the December ELPA21 insert: an eight-page black-and-white pull-out with ELPA21-style reading, listening, writing and speaking practice for grades 9–12, a teacher key with listening scripts, and a family interview in English and Spanish.

o: The November issue: belonging through contribution, 15 lessons, teacher keys.
k: The November 2026 issue of the EL Publishing English Learner Magazine for grades 9–12, themed The Language of Belonging: an editor's letter on designing classrooms for contribution, a two-page teaching feature (access, rehearse, contribute) with Emerging, Progressing and Extension supports, a Native American Heritage Month source-inquiry page, a reading lab (The Table We Built), a voice studio with listening script and speaking performance, a language workshop on because/but/so and word-building, a literary lens (The Empty Chair), writing and visual-literacy tasks, community pages with student publishing and a bilingual family page, a 90-minute lesson plus a 15-lesson November sequence, an original check with rubric, and teacher keys with feedback and reteaching guidance. Web page with every page previewed, plus the free 26-page PDF.

o: Sixteen plates for the teacher who never planned to teach language.
k: "For the teacher who never planned to teach language." Sixteen plates on working with English learners in the general-education classroom.

o: The first issue of the EL Publishing teacher magazine: every teacher is a language teacher.
k: Issue No. 1 of the EL Publishing teacher magazine (Fall 2026): Every Teacher Is a Language Teacher. The founding issue for content teachers who never planned to teach language, with a web edition and the free PDF.

t: Every Teacher Is a Language Teacher
o: Self-paced PD that fits a department meeting. Six sections, no facilitator.
k: Self-paced professional development for general- and special-education teachers: six sections on supporting English learners in any classroom.

o: For the newcomer who is also new to school: find the schooling gap in week one, then the first thirty days.
k: For students with limited or interrupted formal education (SLIFE, SIFE): what the term means and does not mean, a twelve-question schooling interview in English and Spanish with audio, a home-language writing sample and a no-English numbers check, seven signs to look for, the first thirty days week by week, six teaching principles including oral before print and direct reading instruction for teenagers, how to build the schedule and talk about credits and attending until age 21, and a printable one-page note for content teachers.

o: Six years an EL and stuck at Writing 2: a roster finder, a 30-minute diagnostic, twelve weeks on the academic register.
k: For EL and content teachers: who long-term English learners are and why they are stuck, a roster finder that flags six-plus-year and at-risk students, a thirty-minute diagnostic that names one of four profiles, a twelve-week clinic on the academic register (one language feature a week — sentence combining, nominalization, transitions, evidence, hedging, counterclaim — taught on the student's own content reading), two moves for content teachers, a bilingual student letter and a twelve-week tracker that stays in the browser.

o: A page-turning issue: four domain features, daily routines with a live timer, sixteen test moves, coaches who read aloud.
k: An interactive EL Publishing special issue on teaching Mississippi's English Language Proficiency Test (ELPA21) in grades 9–12, read as a page-turning magazine: a cover, contents and masthead, an editor's letter, the ELPT at a glance (four domains, five levels, the determination rule), a November-to-window calendar with a countdown you set once, and four feature articles — Reading, Writing, Listening and Speaking — each with a domain coach who reads the pages aloud, a timed daily routine (25-minute read, 20-minute write, 15-minute listen, 10-minute talk) that runs on a live step timer, six skills taught explicitly with sentence frames, Newcomer/Emerging/Progressing/Challenge lanes you can spotlight, and the four test moves per domain with device rehearsal and anxiety language. A pull-out page collects all sixteen test moves for the wall, and a Before-the-window checklist remembers what is done. Page turns with sound, swipe or arrow keys, a full-screen Present mode for faculty meetings, a Midnight theme, and a stacked Reader mode on phones. No account, nothing leaves the device.

o: Twelve language functions across four grade bands and four proficiency tiers.
k: Twelve language functions across four grade bands and four proficiency tiers: calendar themes, daily plans, texts with quizzes, a standards crosswalk, a sentence-frame ladder and a bilingual student tracker.

o: The year week by week in two lanes, built back from the ELPT window.
k: One theme calendar, two language lanes. Eight units mapped week by week with grammar ladders, ELP and MS CCRS codes, writing products, ELPA21 mirror tasks, a 90-minute block template and an assessment calendar built back from the ELPT window — every recommendation tagged by evidence strength.

t: Six Southern Pies: an ELPA21 Task Set
o: One infographic, all four ELPA21 domains, every task in four lanes.
k: A ready-to-print practice set built from one infographic of six Southern pies, in the formats of the ELPA21: three listening scripts (listen and match, a short conversation, a short lecture on why custards set), a reading passage with five test-style items and a procedure to sequence, four writing tasks from labels and frames to a compare-and-contrast paragraph and an opinion essay or email, and four speaking tasks (observe and report, give the steps, classroom chat, opinion). Every task is laned Newcomer / Emerging / Progressing / Challenge. With a 27-word English–Spanish word list for a cognate hunt, answer key, scoring notes in the spirit of the ELPA21 rubrics, a 90-minute run sheet and MS ELP Standards 1–10 alignment. Toggle student pages, teacher pages or a single domain before printing. Grades 6–12.

t: One Text. Four Lanes. Five Ways to Prove It.
o: One 90-minute block taken apart, decision by decision.
k: The 90-minute arc, the lane-by-lane differentiation and the reasoning behind a Storm Studio block, built on the How Tamales Are Made lesson. Read it before you run your first block.

o: The week a student arrives, hour by hour, ending in an exit ticket.
k: The week a student arrives, hour by hour where it matters: the before-day-one checklist, the walkthrough script, the buddy brief, the family call, which Newcomer Series resource to use each day, and a day-5 exit ticket that tells you the week worked.

o: Drafts itself from the levels; a checklist shows what a Mississippi LSP still needs.
k: Enter the four ELPT levels and the Language Service Plan drafts itself: lane, services, program minutes, instructional and assessment accommodations, a goal with strategies and evidence for each domain, the test-coordinator note and the review note — every drafted field marked and editable, nothing you type ever overwritten — suggested from the level or chosen from an ELPA21 goal bank of 80 measurable goals, each tied to an ELP Standard. Every component a Mississippi LSP is expected to carry is on the form — the identification trail (Home Language Survey, screener and parent notification, each dated and checked against the 30-day clock), ELPT history by year, dual-identification coordination, grading and retention safeguards, nine-weeks reviews, four-year monitoring, the Student Evaluation Team signature block — and a live checklist says what is still missing before it goes for signatures. Print, or save as a file to reopen at review. Prints in English, Spanish, Vietnamese or Arabic for the family copy, and prints a one-page accommodations sheet for the test coordinator.

o: Type the student once; the profile, the plan and the letter fill themselves.
k: Type the student once; open the EL Student Profile, the Language Service Plan and the identification letter already filled in. Lane and overall determination compute as you type. Save the student as one file; reopen it at the semester review.

o: The one page a substitute or a new content teacher needs about a student.
k: Type the ELPT levels and a few facts; get the one page a sub or a new content teacher needs — what the student can do in each domain, the lane, what helps every day, strengths, watch-fors, LSP accommodations, and who to call. For the sub folder.

t: What's New in Teaching English Learners
o: Eight ideas shaping the year, each tagged by how strong the evidence is.
k: Eight ideas shaping 2026 — Science of Reading "yes AND," cross-linguistic transfer, Key Language Uses, newcomer programs, co-teaching, AI, and Mississippi's four-domain exit — each tagged by evidence strength, with sources.

o: Read-aloud scripts, keys, look-fors, and a four-lane version of every task.
